tasks.short: Match the supplier invoice to the order and book it in AFAS.

today.trigger: A supplier invoice arrives by mail, as a PDF, or in one of the three staffing-agency portals, and a bookkeeper sits down to book it.
steps: Open the invoice from Outlook, the scan folder or the agency portal.
Find the purchase order, the warehouse receipt or the transport order.
Compare supplier, quantity, price and VAT, including the G-rekening split on agency invoices.
Type the invoice into AFAS Profit and attach the PDF.
Mail the site or the supplier when the order, the receipt or the hours are missing.
drudgery: Retyping invoice number, IBAN, lines and VAT from a PDF that already shows them.
Searching three inboxes and three portals for the matching order.
Chasing Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo for a receipt that was never entered.
today.time_sinks: Most of the hour goes on finding the order and retyping lines, and only a little goes on a real price or quantity difference.

lenses.faster: For every invoice inside the agreed tolerance, reading the PDF, finding the order and typing the lines drops out. The bookkeeper's hour goes to invoices that differ.
lenses.autonomous: A Peppol message, a mailbox invoice or an agency file starts the match when it arrives. The work waits for a document, and for a person only when the rule stops.
lenses.ambitious: Every supplier invoice, including small warehouse bills and all three agencies, would be matched on the day it arrives, with hours and the G-rekening split checked each time. That is the version of invoices processed without touch that the close can trust.
lenses.joy: Retyping invoice numbers and hunting for purchase orders is work nobody will miss. What remains is a real difference: a price, missing pallets, or hours a site lead rejects.
lenses.options: Each break shows three treatments with the euro effect: post the invoice, post the order and short-pay the difference, or hold the invoice and ask the site.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the tolerance, the match rules and the reason codes, and reviews a sample of invoices that posted on their own.
reach: Accountant: draft the received-not-invoiced accrual from receipts that still have no invoice.
Controller: follow the share of invoices processed without touch, by supplier and by site.

tasks.human_edge: A person still has to settle a commercial difference the rule cannot price: damaged goods, waiting time, fuel surcharge, or agency hours the site says were not worked. The bookkeeper knows which site lead can confirm that.
tasks.pattern_why: The hard step is turning a PDF or a portal invoice into lines with a supplier, a VAT amount and an IBAN. After that, matching to the order and the receipt is a rule AFAS can apply. A clean match posts on its own; a break leaves the workflow with a reason.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice arrives in the AFAS purchase inbox by e-invoice, email or an agency-portal file.
steps: Read supplier, invoice number, lines, VAT and IBAN into fields on the invoice.
Match the lines to the purchase order and the receipt, and reject a duplicate invoice number or an unknown IBAN.
On an agency invoice, compare hours, rate and the G-rekening amount with the portal file.
Post the invoice when quantity, price and VAT sit inside the controller's tolerance, and park it for the payment run.
Put every other invoice in one queue with the euro difference and the suggested cause.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper clears anything outside tolerance, any duplicate or unknown IBAN, and any agency invoice whose hours or G-rekening split differ from the portal. A second person releases the Rabobank payment batch.
data_needed: Purchase order and goods receipt, or the site file that stands in for them.
Supplier invoice as a structured e-invoice or a PDF.
Agency hour file and the agreed G-rekening treatment per agency.
Tolerance for price, quantity and VAT, and the supplier master with VAT number and IBAN.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS purchase-invoice dossier, with the rule version, the match result and the name of anyone who posted by hand.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit records purchase invoices against purchase orders and routes them through an approval workflow.
Microsoft AI Builder extracts header and line fields from invoice PDFs into a structured record.
Dutch hirers often pay part of a staffing-agency invoice to a G-rekening to cover wage tax and VAT, and a wrong split can leave the hirer liable.

risks: A wide tolerance posts a wrong price or a duplicate, and the payment run sends the money before the sample catches it.
An agency invoice posted with the wrong G-rekening split can leave Noordhaven liable for wage tax and VAT as hirer.
Sending invoice images to a tool outside the company's processing agreement can breach AVG where the supplier is a sole trader or the PDF names an employee.
research_questions: Of the last 200 supplier invoices, how many already had a purchase order and a receipt in AFAS, and how many were a PDF with no order?
What price and quantity tolerance would the controller and the auditor accept for an invoice nobody opens?
Do the three agency portals export hours, rate, VAT and G-rekening amount as a stable file, and how often do the sites dispute those hours?
How many payments last quarter went to a duplicate invoice or to an IBAN that had changed?

tasks.short: Book the debits and credits and make the totals agree.

today.trigger: During the day, and again at month end, the bookkeeper posts entries and checks that the accounts add up.
steps: Take amounts from accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, the bank file or a site workbook.
Enter the debits and credits in AFAS or in an Excel sheet that mirrors AFAS.
Total the accounts and compare the sheet with the ledger.
Correct lines until the two totals agree.
Save the workbook on SharePoint for the controller's close file.
drudgery: Re-keying amounts that already sit in an AFAS subledger.
Rebuilding a totals tab so it agrees with the trial balance.
Keeping a workbook that has become a second set of books.
today.time_sinks: Time goes to typing lines AFAS already holds and to making Excel agree with the ledger before anyone will use the figures.

lenses.faster: Subledger totals and known recurring amounts post in AFAS with no spreadsheet between them. Building a fresh totals workbook each month drops out.
lenses.autonomous: Recurring entries for rent, leases, insurance and agreed accruals post on the close calendar. A control total that fails opens a task that night.
lenses.ambitious: A trial balance by Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo would be ready every morning, so the forecast uses the same numbers as the books. The company would finally have one set of figures during the month, which it does not have today.
lenses.joy: Adding columns to prove a workbook still agrees with AFAS is work nobody will miss. Choosing a one-off correction, and seeing that the month makes sense, stays.
lenses.options: Before a one-off entry posts, show the effect on the site result and on the VAT position beside the proposed booking.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the recurring entries and their control totals, and treats AFAS as the only ledger the forecast may use.
reach: FP&A Analyst: take site actuals from AFAS for the forecast, from the same trial balance the books use.
Accountant: take standard accruals from a schedule that already posts, and spend time on entries that need judgment.

tasks.human_edge: Someone still has to decide that a one-off is the right picture of the month: a claim, a credit, or a correction the subledgers cannot know. The arithmetic belongs to AFAS.
tasks.pattern_why: Debits, credits and totals follow the chart of accounts and the posting rules. AFAS already does this when the entry starts inside a subledger. The work left is to turn recurring amounts into scheduled journals and to stop rebuilding them in Excel.

in_practice.trigger: A subledger approves a batch, or the close calendar reaches a recurring entry such as rent or a known accrual.
steps: Post subledger batches to the general ledger with their own control total.
Post recurring journals from a schedule that names the account, the site, the amount and the end date.
Leave a one-off entry on a short queue with the supporting document attached.
Block the posting when the batch total differs from the source.
Refresh the Power BI extract from the same ledger the next night.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper posts one-off entries and clears a failed control total. The controller samples recurring journals each month. Rule changes are logged under a second name.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and the three site cost centres.
Schedule of recurring amounts with an owner and an end date.
Source batch totals from AP, AR, payroll and the bank.
The list of manual journals the bookkeepers actually posted last quarter.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS journal log, with the schedule version and the name on any manual line, kept with the month-close file on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit posts subledger transactions and journals to the general ledger and produces a trial balance by account and cost centre.
Rent, insurance, lease and similar accruals follow a dated schedule that a posting rule can apply until the end date.

risks: A recurring journal keeps posting after the contract has changed, and the monthly sample is too thin to see it.
Site leads and FP&A keep using a workbook, so the forecast and the ledger diverge again.
A bookkeeper who can both change a recurring rule and pass the result weakens the segregation the auditor expects.
research_questions: How many journal lines did the bookkeepers type last month, and how many of those repeated a figure AFAS already held?
Which amounts recur every month with a known account, site and end date?
Did any audit adjustment last year come from a spreadsheet total that differed from the ledger?

tasks.short: Put each amount on the right account, site and VAT code.

today.trigger: An invoice or a journal line has to be filed under a ledger account, a site and a VAT code before it can be posted.
steps: Read the invoice text or the line description.
Choose the general-ledger account, the site cost centre and the VAT code.
Check the supplier country and whether the reverse charge applies.
Post the coded lines in AFAS.
Repair codes that the VAT return or the accountant later rejects.
drudgery: Looking up the same supplier's account and VAT code that was used last month.
Splitting a single invoice across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo by guesswork.
Correcting VAT codes after the return has been drafted.
today.time_sinks: Time goes to repeating last month's coding and to fixing site and VAT choices that three people make in three different ways.

lenses.faster: A supplier with a confirmed rule takes the account, the site and the VAT code without a fresh lookup. Only new wording waits for a person.
lenses.autonomous: Coding runs when the invoice is captured. A known rule posts with the match. A new combination waits for one confirmation and then becomes the rule.
lenses.ambitious: Costs would hit the right site and the right VAT code the first time, including agency labour and cross-border transport. The forecast and the VAT return would start from figures nobody has to rebuild at close.
lenses.joy: Repeating the same supplier code all day is work nobody will miss. A new supplier, or a lane whose VAT treatment is genuinely unclear, stays interesting.
lenses.options: Where the text fits two VAT treatments, show domestic VAT and reverse charge side by side, with the effect on the VAT return and on the site cost.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the coding rules and the supplier master, and reviews the short list of new combinations.
reach: FP&A Analyst: use costs split across the three sites in the week they are incurred.
Accountant: review the new VAT combinations as a short list before the return is filed.

tasks.human_edge: The first time a supplier, a lane or a mixed-site invoice appears, a person has to say which site consumed the cost and which VAT treatment is right. The bookkeeper is the one who can ask the site lead and read the contract clause.
tasks.pattern_why: Invoice wording is unstructured, and the output is a closed set: an account that exists, one of three sites, and a VAT code the supplier's country allows. A person confirms a new combination once. After that the rule posts on its own and the check is mechanical.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice line is captured and has no confirmed coding rule for that supplier and wording.
steps: Propose the ledger account, the site and the VAT code from the supplier history and the line text.
Accept the proposal automatically when it matches a confirmed rule and the VAT code is allowed for that supplier.
Hold a new combination, or any reverse-charge and cross-border transport line, for the bookkeeper.
On confirmation, store the combination as the rule for the next invoice.
List every new rule for the accountant before the VAT return is filed.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper confirms each new supplier, site split or VAT treatment. The accountant reviews the list of new rules before the VAT return. Existing rules post with the invoice.
data_needed: Chart of accounts, site cost centres and the allowed VAT codes.
Supplier master with country and VAT number.
At least a year of posted lines by supplier, used as confirmed history.
The contract note that says when transport is reverse-charged or zero-rated.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS coding rule log: who confirmed the rule, the invoice it came from, and every later line that used it.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit stores general-ledger accounts, cost centres and VAT codes on a purchase invoice and uses them in the VAT return.
A supplier's past coding predicts the next invoice often enough that a proposal plus a human confirmation of new cases is a workable control.
Cross-border transport and the reverse charge are a known source of VAT corrections when the code is copied from a domestic invoice.

risks: A wrong VAT code on transport posts quietly and comes back as an audit adjustment or a VAT correction.
A rule that always picks the previous site mis-states Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, and the forecast that uses those actuals.
One careless confirmation becomes the rule for every later invoice from that supplier.
research_questions: What share of invoice lines last month used the same account, site and VAT code as that supplier's previous invoice?
How many VAT codes were corrected on the last two returns, and were the corrections on transport or on agency invoices?
Can each cost be tied to one site from the order, or do many invoices cover more than one site?

tasks.short: Move the journal totals into the general ledger.

today.trigger: A source journal is ready and someone copies the totals into the general ledger before the close can start.
steps: Export payroll, the bank book, a site sheet, or a cleared AP or AR list.
Map the totals to general-ledger accounts and to the three sites.
Enter or import the lines into AFAS.
Compare the source total with the ledger total.
Correct the gap before the controller opens the close.
drudgery: Pasting the same payroll and bank totals into the ledger each period.
Rebuilding a mapping that lives in someone's workbook.
Re-checking control totals that a posting interface could compare on its own.
today.time_sinks: Time goes to export, paste and re-check, so that payroll, bank and site figures land on the right ledger accounts before the close.

lenses.faster: The export, paste and re-total between payroll, bank, payables, receivables and the general ledger drops out. One control total per source remains.
lenses.autonomous: An approved subledger posts to the general ledger on approval. A difference in the control total stops that source and alerts the bookkeeper the same day.
lenses.ambitious: Every subledger would tie to the general ledger every night. The month would open on a ledger that already ties, which is the condition for a shorter close.
lenses.joy: Copying figures from one screen into another is work nobody will miss. Refusing a source that does not tie, and getting it fixed, stays.
lenses.options: When a source misses its control total, show the gap split by site, by VAT code and by the agency clearing account.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the posting map and the tie-out, and the daily work is a source that failed its control total.
reach: Controller: open the close on a ledger that already ties to payroll, the bank, payables and receivables.
Payroll Specialist: hand over an approved payroll journal that posts itself to the agreed accounts.

tasks.human_edge: A person still refuses a source whose own total is wrong, especially payroll and the agency clearing account. Accepting a neat import of a bad file would make the ledger look finished when it is not.
tasks.pattern_why: Moving a balanced journal into the general ledger is a mapping and a control total. The inputs are structured, and the output either ties or it does not. A model adds nothing once the map is written down.

in_practice.trigger: Payroll is approved, the bank book is matched, or an AP or AR batch is released.
steps: Send the source batch to the general ledger through the AFAS posting the module already supports.
Compare the source total, the VAT total and the site split with the ledger.
Park the batch when any of those totals differ.
Write a new account or a new allowance to a named suspense account with an owner.
Leave a one-line tie-out for the controller at the start of the close.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper releases a batch that failed its control total, after the source owner corrects it. The controller reads the tie-out before the close is signed.
data_needed: The posting map from each source account to the general ledger and the site.
Control totals from payroll, bank, AP, AR and the agency clearing account.
A named owner for each suspense account.
The list of journals the bookkeepers still copy by hand.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS posting log for the batch, plus the monthly tie-out stored in the close folder on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit posts approved subledger batches from payables, receivables, payroll and banks into the general ledger.
A batch import that must hit a control total, and that parks the batch when it misses, is ordinary accounting software.

risks: A payroll or agency file that misses its own total can still be forced in, and the close then starts from a dirty ledger.
A new allowance or a new surcharge falls into a suspense account that nobody has been given to clear.
The sites keep private workbooks, so FP&A rebuilds a second set of figures beside the ledger.
research_questions: Which sources are still copied by hand into the general ledger, and which already post inside AFAS?
Do the three site workbooks follow one layout with stable account codes?
What single control total would the controller accept as proof that a source has landed in full?

tasks.short: Reconcile the accounts and write up the differences.

today.trigger: The Rabobank statement arrives, or month end starts, and the balance in AFAS differs from the bank or from a subledger.
steps: Download the Rabobank statement and import it, or work from the PDF.
Match receipts and payments to open customer and supplier items.
Tick the lines that agree and list the lines that stay open.
Ask a site, a customer or another bookkeeper what the odd line is.
Write the remaining differences on the reconciliation in the close file.
drudgery: Ticking statement lines against open items one by one.
Rewriting the same timing difference on the reconciliation every month.
Hunting through Outlook for the customer's payment reference.
today.time_sinks: Time goes to lines that do match, and to writing timing differences again, before the few breaks that actually change the result get any attention.

lenses.faster: Lines with a clear invoice reference match on their own when the statement is imported. The remaining time sits in the short list of breaks and in one written reason for each.
lenses.autonomous: The morning Rabobank file starts the match as soon as it is in AFAS. Open breaks are on a list before anyone asks for the reconciliation.
lenses.ambitious: The bank, customer receipts, pallet deposits and the three agency clearing accounts would be reconciled every week. Breaks would be small when the close starts, and cash would hit the right invoice while days sales outstanding still means something.
lenses.joy: Ticking a statement line by line is work nobody will miss. Finding out why a customer short-paid, and whether the difference is real, stays.
lenses.options: For each break, set out three amounts: a timing difference, a posting error and a real loss. The bookkeeper accepts one of them.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the cash-application rules and the catalogue of break reasons, and signs the accounts that still move.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: take the unmatched customer receipts, with the invoice the payment almost fitted.
Accountant: book small agreed differences inside a limit the controller has set.

tasks.human_edge: A person still has to say that a short-pay is a real dispute, a bank charge, or a payment on the wrong entity, and what the controller should be told. The match can group the lines. It cannot make that call.
tasks.pattern_why: The match itself is a rule on structured bank lines, but the work crosses Rabobank, AFAS open items and sometimes an agency portal, and it ends in a written reason. The reconciliation counts only when a person signs it. That is a gated flow, with the person on the breaks and on the sign-off.

in_practice.trigger: The daily Rabobank CAMT file arrives, or a clearing account is due its weekly tie-out.
steps: Import the statement and match lines to open items on invoice number, amount and IBAN.
Apply the matched customer receipts and supplier payments.
Group what is left as timing, possible duplicate, unknown receipt or real difference.
Draft one sentence per open break from the line text and the closest open item.
Put the reconciliation on the bookkeeper's list for sign-off, with material breaks marked for the controller.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper signs each reconciliation before it is part of the close. The controller signs breaks above a set amount and any write-off. Cash is applied to a specific invoice only when the reference meets the rule.
data_needed: Rabobank CAMT.053 or MT940 file, on the contract the company already has.
Open customer and supplier items with invoice numbers.
Clearing accounts for agencies, pallet deposits and suspense.
The controller's limit for a bookkeeper write-off and for a controller sign-off.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS bank-match log and the signed reconciliation in the SharePoint close folder, with the reason code on every open line.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit imports Dutch bank statements and proposes matches against open items.
Rabobank business accounts can deliver CAMT.053 statements and pain.001 payment files.
BlackLine prepares account reconciliations with match rules and a separate reviewer sign-off.

risks: Cash applied to the wrong invoice hides a dispute and makes days sales outstanding look better than it is.
Many small timing differences, written off one by one, add up to an audit adjustment.
A drafted explanation that is signed unread becomes a false record in the close file.
research_questions: On last month's Rabobank statement, what share of lines matched an open item on the first pass, and what were the top five causes of the rest?
Do customer payments carry the invoice number often enough to apply cash with a rule?
Which open breaks last quarter were timing differences that cleared within a month, and which changed the result or days sales outstanding?

tasks.short: Get the payroll figures ready and into the books.

today.trigger: The pay cycle is due and hours, allowances and absence have to become payroll figures and a journal.
steps: Collect hours, overtime and shift allowances from Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Check the names against AFAS and against absence recorded by HR.
Pass the pack to the Payroll Specialist and answer the questions that come back.
After the approved run, check the payroll journal and post it to the general ledger.
Compare net pay with the Rabobank salary batch.
drudgery: Chasing three sites for shift sheets in three layouts.
Retyping allowances the CAO table could calculate from approved hours.
Tying the net-pay file to the bank batch with a calculator and a sheet.
today.time_sinks: Time goes to collecting hours and allowances from the sites and retyping them, before the Payroll Specialist can even start the run.

lenses.faster: Where AFAS already holds time and absence, chasing site sheets and retyping allowances drops out. The bookkeeper checks the exceptions and the journal tie-out.
lenses.autonomous: On the payroll calendar a draft input and a draft journal are waiting for the Payroll Specialist. After approval, net pay is compared with the Rabobank batch on its own.
lenses.ambitious: Every own-staff allowance would be checked against the correct CAO table before the run, and flex labour would stay on the agency invoice, coded to the right site. The close would have a payroll journal that does not need to be reopened.
lenses.joy: Chasing spreadsheets of hours is work nobody will miss. Spotting a shift that cannot be right, and leaving the pay decision with the Payroll Specialist, stays.
lenses.options: Show this run beside the previous run by site and by CAO group, and list the allowances that moved and the euro effect of each.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper keeps the tie-out between AFAS Payroll, the general ledger and the salary batch, and keeps the list of inputs that still arrive late from the sites.
reach: Payroll Specialist: start the run from a checked input, and spend the cycle on CAO questions and absence.
Accountant: reconcile the payroll control account to the paid batch in the same week as payday.

tasks.human_edge: The Payroll Specialist owns the pay decision under both CAOs, including sickness pay and Wet verbetering poortwachter. The bookkeeper's edge is spotting hours that cannot be right and keeping flex-agency cost out of the payroll journal.
tasks.pattern_why: The calculation belongs to AFAS Payroll once hours and wage components are approved. Getting there crosses three sites, HR absence and a specialist who must release every run. The bookkeeper's slice is preparation and the tie-out, and it counts only after that approval.

in_practice.trigger: The payroll calendar opens the input window for the next run.
steps: Pull approved hours, overtime and absence from AFAS for own staff on both CAO groups.
Flag site lines that still arrive outside AFAS, and flag hours that clash with recorded absence.
Price the standard allowances from the CAO components already configured, and hold anything the table does not name.
Hand the Payroll Specialist a draft input and, after the run, a journal by site.
Match the approved net-pay total to the Rabobank salary batch and post the journal when it ties.
in_practice.human_gate: The Payroll Specialist approves every pay run. The bookkeeper signs the tie-out to the bank and the ledger. A second person releases the salary payment at Rabobank. Flex workers stay on the agency invoice.
data_needed: Own-staff hours and absence in AFAS, split by the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO.
The site files that still carry overtime and allowances, and their column layout.
Configured wage components and the payroll journal map by site.
The approved net-pay batch and the Rabobank pain.001 total.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS Payroll run log and the journal posting log, with the tie-out to the Rabobank batch stored in the payroll close folder.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit Payroll calculates wages from hours and configured wage components and can produce a journal and a payment file.
A Dutch works council has a consent right over arrangements for systems that process personnel data, which covers a new tool reading hours and absence.
Using a model to decide payable hours from sickness notes would sit near the employment uses covered by the EU AI Act, beyond a calculation from hours HR has already approved.

risks: The transport CAO table applied to warehouse staff, or the reverse, pays the wrong allowance.
A rule that judges sickness hours cuts across Wet verbetering poortwachter records owned by HR and the Payroll Specialist.
A new tool that reads absence and hours needs a privacy assessment and can need works council consent before it is switched on.
The person who prepares the input must not be the only person who can release the salary batch.
research_questions: Which payroll inputs still arrive as site spreadsheets, and which are already in AFAS time and absence?
Does the Payroll Specialist want the bookkeeper to prepare inputs, or only to tie the approved journal to the bank batch?
Are the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO already separate employee groups in AFAS Payroll?
Are all flex workers billed by the agencies, with none paid on the Noordhaven payroll?

tasks.short: Make the customer invoices and the statements.

today.trigger: Work has been delivered and the billing cycle, weekly or at month end, is due.
steps: Collect trips, pallet-weeks, handling and surcharges from the site files.
Look up the customer rate and the VAT treatment.
Create the invoice in AFAS with the mandatory invoice fields.
Send the invoice by Outlook.
Build an account statement when the customer or the Credit and Collections Officer asks.
drudgery: Copying quantities out of site workbooks into the invoice screen.
Looking up the same rate card for the same customer every cycle.
Rebuilding statements that are already the open items in AFAS.
today.time_sinks: Time goes to gathering quantities and retyping them, then to producing the PDF and the statement by hand.

lenses.faster: Pricing from the rate card and creating the invoice and the statement drops out for standard lines. Gathering quantities remains only where a site file is incomplete.
lenses.autonomous: A complete delivery file from a site, or the billing calendar, starts the invoice run. Standard invoices go out on that run.
lenses.ambitious: Customers would be invoiced in the week the work was done, including the surcharges the contract already names. Days sales outstanding would then be counted from a real delivery date, for warehouse storage and for transport.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the same invoice from a rate card and a site sheet is work nobody will miss. A surcharge the contract does not name, and the credit note after a real dispute, stays.
lenses.options: For a shipment that fits more than one VAT treatment, show both invoices with the VAT amount, and hold them until one is chosen.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the rate card, the billing calendar and the quantity file the sites must send, and reviews the lines the rule held back.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: send the account statement from the same run that issued the invoices.
FP&A Analyst: see invoiced revenue by site in the week the invoice is raised.

tasks.human_edge: A person still has to price work the rate card does not name, and to agree a credit note when the customer disputes the quantity. Issuing a VAT invoice with a guessed rate would create the next credit note.
tasks.pattern_why: A standard invoice is the contract rate times a delivered quantity, with the VAT treatment taken from the customer and the lane. Dutch invoice fields are fixed. Once the quantity file and the rate card sit in AFAS, the run is a rule. Lines the card does not cover wait for a person.

in_practice.trigger: A site delivers the agreed quantity file, or the billing calendar falls due.
steps: Load quantities per customer, site and service: trips, pallet-weeks, handling and named surcharges.
Price them from the rate card and apply the VAT treatment stored on the contract.
Issue and send invoices whose lines all sit on the card, with consecutive numbering and the required VAT text.
Hold lines with no rate, a quantity far outside the recent pattern, or a cross-border VAT question.
Produce the open-item statement for the Credit and Collections Officer from the same run.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper releases held lines and every credit note. The controller sets the quantity band that may pass on its own. Standard invoices on the rate card go out on the calendar.
data_needed: A quantity file per site with a stable layout, or the same data already in AFAS.
Customer rate cards, including named surcharges and the VAT treatment.
Customer master with VAT number, invoice address and any portal they require.
The recent pattern of quantities used to flag an outlier.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS sales-invoice log, including the rate-card version and the quantity file name, with held lines and credit notes signed on the dossier.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit creates sales invoices and customer statements from orders or billing lines and can send them by email or as an e-invoice.
A Dutch VAT invoice needs consecutive numbering, the supplier and customer VAT details and the correct VAT treatment, which a billing run can fill from master data.

risks: An invoice issued from a bad quantity file is a VAT document, and the credit note that follows hurts the relationship and the days-sales-outstanding figure.
Cross-border transport VAT, copied from the previous domestic invoice, creates a correction on the VAT return.
A customer that requires its own portal will not start the payment term from an email PDF.
research_questions: Where are delivered quantities recorded today, and can they be exported per customer, site and service?
What share of invoice lines last month was a contract rate times a quantity, and what share was a price someone typed?
How many credit notes last quarter came from a wrong quantity or a wrong VAT treatment?
Which customers require a portal upload, and does that portal set the invoice date used for days sales outstanding?

tasks.short: Make the purchase orders and the expense claims.

today.trigger: A site needs to buy something, or an employee hands in receipts, and the bookkeeper turns that into a purchase order or an expense report.
steps: Receive the request or the receipts by Outlook or Teams.
Check the amount, the receipt, the site and whether policy on SharePoint covers it.
Type the purchase order or the expense lines in AFAS or in Excel.
Send the pack to the budget holder for approval.
Chase missing receipts and signatures, then code and post what is approved.
drudgery: Typing purchase orders from short emails sent by warehouse leads.
Rebuilding an expense sheet from photographed receipts.
Sending reminder mails for a missing receipt, cost centre or signature.
today.time_sinks: Time goes to turning mail into documents and to chasing what is incomplete, before a budget holder has even approved the spend.

lenses.faster: Typing a purchase order from an email, and rebuilding an expense sheet from receipts, drops out. The bookkeeper deals with missing receipts, new suppliers and policy breaks.
lenses.autonomous: A request from a site lead, or an expense submitted with a receipt, starts coding and the approval route. A complete, in-policy item reaches the budget holder without being retyped.
lenses.ambitious: Every purchase would have an order before the invoice arrives, and expenses would fall in the month they were incurred. The payables match would then succeed on the first pass, which is what lifts the share of invoices processed without touch.
lenses.joy: Retyping receipts and chasing a missing signature is work nobody will miss. A doubtful claim, or a new supplier bank account, stays worth a person's look.
lenses.options: Where a receipt fits two sites or two cost centres, show both codings with the budget each would use.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the expense rules, the approval limits and the checklist for a new supplier, and reviews what the rules reject.
reach: Controller: see purchase commitments by site before the invoice arrives.
HR Administrator: point staff to one expense route that already checks the receipt and the cost centre.

tasks.human_edge: A budget holder still approves the commitment. The bookkeeper still checks a claim that breaks policy and still starts a new supplier, because a changed IBAN is a fraud control and needs a second person.
tasks.pattern_why: A purchase order from an approved request is a rule, while a receipt photo is unstructured. The flow crosses the site lead, AFAS, the receipt and the budget holder, and it counts only after that person approves. The bookkeeper sees the items the rule cannot pass.

in_practice.trigger: A site lead submits a purchase request, or an employee submits an expense with a receipt photo.
steps: Read the request or the receipt into supplier, date, amount, VAT and site.
Check it against the expense policy and the remaining approval limit of the budget holder.
Create the purchase order or the expense claim in AFAS and route it to that budget holder.
Return anything with no receipt, no site or a policy break to the sender with the missing item named.
After approval, code from the confirmed rules and hold a new supplier, or a new IBAN, for a second person.
in_practice.human_gate: The budget holder approves each purchase order and each expense before it counts. A second person, who is not the requester, confirms a new supplier IBAN. The bookkeeper clears policy breaks and incomplete receipts.
data_needed: The expense policy and the approval matrix by amount and site.
Receipt images and the purchase request text.
Supplier master and the IBAN already on file.
AFAS declarations, or a clear reason it is not used today.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS workflow log on the purchase order or the expense claim: submitter, approver, coding rule and any IBAN check, with the receipt stored on the dossier.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports purchase orders, commitment recording and employee expense declarations with a receipt and an approval workflow.
Microsoft AI Builder can read total, date, supplier and tax amount from a receipt or invoice image.
A new flow that reads employee receipts processes personal data and can require works council involvement under the WOR before it is introduced.

risks: A purchase order created from a loose email can commit the company when the budget-holder step is skipped or defaulted.
A changed supplier IBAN on a new order is a common fraud path and fails if one person can both enter it and approve it.
Scanning employee receipts in a tool outside the processing agreement is an AVG issue and can require works council consent.
People who submit expenses late will still distort the month. A cleaner form does not by itself move the submission date.
research_questions: What share of purchase invoices last month had a purchase order that was raised before the invoice arrived?
Is AFAS expense declaration already available, and what stops people at the three sites from using it?
Which expense types does policy pass with a receipt and a budget holder, and which need an extra check under the CAO?
Has the works council already been consulted on tools that read employee receipts?

role.altitude: Owner of the procure-to-pay and order-to-cash rules in AFAS: match tolerances, VAT and site coding, rate cards, billing calendars and the exception queues. The job is measured by days to close, invoices processed without touch, days sales outstanding, and audit adjustments that start in the subledgers.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: routine account statements and the list of receipts that could not be applied, leaving disputes and payment plans with that officer.
Accountant: standard accruals, prepayments and small agreed reconciliation items from schedules the controller has set.
Payroll Specialist: a checked input file and the payday tie-out to the ledger and the bank, leaving CAO interpretation and the pay run with the specialist.
Controller: a running list of breaks and commitments during the month, so the close is a review of what is left.
FP&A Analyst: site actuals from the ledger in the week they are posted, as the base for the forecast.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks are about 412 hours a year for each bookkeeper, roughly a quarter of the role, so automating them changes the work and the close and does not by itself remove one of the three seats. The ceiling is the volume of real exceptions: agency hours, transport VAT, warehouse claims and quantities that may live outside AFAS, since no transport or warehouse system is in the stated landscape. Segregation of duties, the statutory audit file, both CAOs, and works-council and AVG duties on employee hours and receipts set the rest of the limit. The useful gain is a close the business trusts, with cleaner actuals for the forecast.
skills_to_grow: Writing and testing AFAS match, coding and billing rules, with a sample the external auditor can follow.
Dutch VAT on domestic warehousing and on cross-border transport, including the reverse charge.
The G-rekening split and the checks on a staffing-agency invoice.
Reading a Rabobank CAMT statement and a payment batch well enough to explain a break.
How to prepare a short works-council and privacy note when a flow reads employee receipts or hours.
Running a weekly exception review with the controller, aimed at fixing the rule that caused the break.
role.ambitious_version: Supplier invoices, agency invoices and customer invoices post themselves inside rules the bookkeeper maintains, the bank matches overnight, and both CAOs feed an approved payroll journal that already ties. The bookkeeper's week is a short exception meeting with the controller and a change to one rule that removes a recurring break. Days to close fall because the subledgers are clean before day one, invoices processed without touch is the number this role manages, and the forecast uses Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo actuals that nobody rebuilt in Excel.
